# Education in Greece
Education in Greece operates within a structured framework that includes Pre-kindergarten (Preschool/Kindergarten), Primary School ($\text{Dimotiko}$), Lower Secondary Education ($\text{Gymnasio}$), and Upper Secondary Education ($\text{Lyceum}$). Pre-kindergarten is compulsory and comprises two years: Pre-kindergarten ($\text{Pronipium}$, ages 4–5) and Kindergarten ($\text{Nipiagogeio}$, ages 5–6). Primary school is compulsory for six years ($\text{Dimotiko}$), running from age 6 to 12.
Lower Secondary Education ($\text{Gymnasio}$) is compulsory until age 15 and consists of three academic years. Upper Secondary Education ($\text{Lyceum}$) is non-compulsory and lasts three years, serving as the equivalent of a high school. The system includes various specialized tracks, such as Vocational Lyceum ($\text{EPAL}$), which offers dual-diploma studies. The National Qualification Framework ($\text{HQF}$) aligns Greek qualifications with the European Qualifications Framework ($\text{EQF}$).
In terms of secondary education, the grading system in upper secondary schools ranges from 1 to 20, where 20 is equivalent to an 'A'. Furthermore, Greece offers non-formal education options, including Open Courses ($\text{GUnet}$) and online training via bodies like the National Centre for Public Administration and Local Government ($\text{EKDDA}$).
